feed.title: Laplace Research
feed.subtitle: Foundation models for calibrated forecasting and evidence-sensitive belief revision.

entry.title: Introducing Laplace Oracle: Our family of models that buy evidence before they forecast
entry.summary: Six open models trained to buy observations, report probabilities and decide when to stop. Every one declined a copied reading, yet every one changed its forecast when that reading was supplied. RL's effect on held-out worlds was uncertain, and a prior-only baseline scored above all six.

entry.title: When thinking helps models believe forged records
entry.summary: In a paired experiment on four open models, thinking mode raised final-answer accuracy by 10 to 34 points and made most models harder to pressure, but every model became worse at rejecting a record pasted into the chat.

entry.title: Signet: open models that check where a record came from before they believe it
entry.summary: Most models accept a fake record pasted into the chat as readily as a genuine tool result. Signet-2B, 4B and 9B adopt genuine records and reject pasted ones, including in formats they never saw in training, and still accept valid corrections.

entry.title: Introducing ConvictionBench: when should a model change its mind?
entry.summary: When challenged, a language model has to keep its answer, revise it, or say the evidence is insufficient. ConvictionBench measures how that decision moves with evidence quality and social pressure across 26,478 generated episodes, released with the Laplace Conviction Series.

entry.title: Tarot-Draw: what model scale changes in binary forecasting, and what it does not
entry.summary: Three binary forecasting models (1.7B, 4B, and 8B) trained on the same 81,870 resolved questions. The 4B matches the 8B within the resolution of the experiment, and the 1.7B is the best calibrated of the three.
